name: Rebels and Founders: How the United States Began
description: From colonial grievances and a war for independence to a written constitution and a new capital: how thirteen colonies became the United States, 1607 to the age of Jackson.

checkpoints.name: Colonies and ideas
checkpoints.note: The Colony of Virginia and the Massachusetts Bay Colony grow into the Thirteen Colonies of the British Empire. Colonists read John Locke and Montesquieu, the voices of the Age of Enlightenment, and Benjamin Franklin becomes the best-known American. The Seven Years' War ends in 1763 with Britain master of eastern North America.

checkpoints.name: The road to war
checkpoints.note: To pay for the war, Parliament taxes the colonies, and their protest at being taxed without a voice in it starts the American Revolution. When the East India Company is given a monopoly on tea, protesters dump a cargo of it into Boston harbour in 1773. Fighting breaks out in 1775 and George Washington takes command.

checkpoints.name: Independence won
checkpoints.note: Thomas Jefferson drafts the Declaration of Independence, adopted on 4 July 1776. In the American Revolutionary War France, won over by Franklin, joins the colonists in 1778, and a British army surrenders in 1781. In the Treaty of Paris of 1783, negotiated by Franklin, John Adams and others, Britain recognises the United States.

checkpoints.name: A more perfect union
checkpoints.note: In 1787 the US Constitution is written, with James Madison as its chief architect, and Alexander Hamilton helps win its approval. In 1789 Washington becomes president, Congress first meets and the Supreme Court is created. The Bill of Rights follows, and Hamilton's Treasury creates the dollar. Yellow fever ravages Philadelphia, then the capital.

checkpoints.name: The young republic
checkpoints.note: Adams moves into the White House in the new city of Washington in 1800. President Jefferson makes the Louisiana Purchase in 1803 and sends Lewis and Clark to the Pacific. In the War of 1812 the USS Constitution wins fame and Andrew Jackson triumphs; his followers found the Democratic Party.
